summary: Wednesday 18 Nov. Themes: workday sleep (ResMed 71%), caffeine plus L-theanine evidence with its limits, FSSAI's October labelling warning, a founder story on the 80 mg caffeine choice and a small-study reality check on the ultrasound sleep patch. LinkedIn is the magnesium ingredient post from the weekly plan. Reddit could not be read live (Chrome not connected), so there are 8 bank comments on label reading, burnout, founder sleep, vitamin D, routines, habits, launching in India and first-coffee timing.

trends.topic: ResMed survey: 71% of Indian workers say poor sleep hurts work; 58% say workload interferes with sleep
Caffeine plus L-theanine improved attention after one night of sleep loss (Brit J Nutr, high dose, one night)
FSSAI October advisory to nutraceutical makers on labelling lapses
trends.angle: Transparency: the pack is a document

trends.topic: Magnesium bisglycinate 250 mg elemental, 4-week RCT: modest self-reported benefit
Wearable ultrasound patch: REM 43 minutes sooner (28 participants)
KSM-66 ashwagandha trials mostly use 600 mg a day; coverage is largely promotional and cortisol results are mixed
trends.angle: Background only. Our Nights has 300 mg, so avoid implying a match; use 'the dose studied' wording

linkedin_trends.topic: FSSAI labelling advisory and NMN notice for supplements
linkedin_trends.angle: The Friday post on what we checked on our own labels

linkedin_competitors.takeaway: Retail and pharma distribution are the growth route. We win on transparency first.
